newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end easier after brief rise on machinery data.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end easier after brief rise on machinery data.

text.p: Key September 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures closed Tuesday slightly easier after shedding earlier gains from weaker-than-expected April machinery orders data.

Japan's private-sector machinery orders, excluding those for machinery at electric power firms and for ships, showed a rise of a seasonally adjusted 7.2 percent in April from the previous month, which compared with economists' forecast of a rise of more than 10 percent.
The September was down 0.06 at 123.14. It briefly rose as high as 123.37 after the release of the data this afternoon.

"The contract failed to rise further because profit-taking emerged at the top," said a dealer at a city bank's securities unit. "It will consolidate at the lower end of 123-124 yen by early next week just before the Bank of Japan (BOJ) releases its key tankan survey."

There was a growing view that the next "tankan" survey due out on June 25, may show corporate sentiment worsening from the previous survey released in April. But the market has not yet fully factored in such speculation, traders said.
In the cash bond market, profit-taking emerged at the long-end of the yield curve including the 190th 10-year JGBs and this capped the September's topside, traders said.
But buying from banks and life insurers continued in the short- to medium-term bonds, they said.
"The recent overshoot resulted in today's sales of the 190th issue," said a senior dealer at another city bank's securities unit.
Expectations that the 190th 10-year JGB may take over benchmark status from the current 182nd issue had fuelled aggressive buying of the 190th bond recently.
The yield of 190th issue rose as high as 2.635 percent on Tuesday, against Monday's finish of 2.595 percent. It stood at 2.590 percent at 0731 GMT.
The current benchmark 182nd was yielding 2.485 percent, up 0.020 from Monday's close.
The Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd set the coupon rate of its June five-year debentures at 2.4 percent on Tuesday, down from 2.5 percent in May.
The coupon rate for Nippon Credit Bank Ltd's June five-year bank debentures was cut to 2.75 percent from 2.95 percent for its May debentures.
